note: Generic example show formats in Crewcut's own words. Your own library in brand/show-formats/formats.json adds to these and replaces formats with the same id. Template paths are relative to this folder.

formats.name: Tool test

kinds.name: Free against paid
kinds.when: A free tool claims to replace a paid one.

kinds.name: Rebuild it yourself
kinds.when: An AI agent can rebuild a paid app or service in a few hours.

kinds.name: Which setting wins
kinds.when: One tool has several modes, models or price tiers to compare on the same task.

formats.when: The input is a tool, an app, a repository or a model the viewer could use or pay for. The video runs the same real task through it and gives a verdict.

structure.name: Opening
structure.purpose: The result first: one sentence with the surprising number, the proof in one line, the viewer's stake (money, data, time), a plan with a count.

structure.name: Unit 1
structure.purpose: The first test: hook with a number, the visible proof, one example, a punch line. It stands alone as a Short.

structure.name: Unit 2
structure.purpose: The second test, higher stakes: where it breaks or surprises. Same hook, proof, punch pattern.

structure.name: Unit 3
structure.purpose: The strongest test last: the one that decides the verdict.

structure.name: Close
structure.purpose: The verdict that picks up sentence 1, then at most one link sentence. No recap, no goodbye.

packaging_rules: The viewer's stake (money, data or time) is in the title; the task itself is shown in the video.
The result must not be predictable from the title.
Three title and thumbnail pairs, each from a named formula.
title_formulas: I tested X so you don't pay for Y
X replaced my Y subscription (here is the catch)
The free X beat the paid Y at one thing
formats.strong: Example format: a measured claim, an own number, where it breaks and a verdict is a common outlier pattern in tech channels. Replace this line with your own evidence.

formats.name: Claim check
formats.when: The input is a viral post, tweet or headline that claims a number or a result the creator can check in minutes.

structure.name: Case
structure.purpose: Sentence 1: the claim against your own number, in first person.

structure.name: Proof
structure.purpose: The visible test: the screen, the log, the clock. Fast.

structure.name: Punch line
structure.purpose: One short sentence the viewer remembers. No ask, no goodbye.

packaging_rules: The claim is quoted in a few words on screen in the first second.
The related video links the long video on the same topic.
title_formulas: Is X really true? I checked
X says Y. My number says Z
formats.strong: Example format: a claim against an own measurement is quick to make and easy to prove.

formats.name: Incident file
formats.when: The input is something that went wrong or surprised you in your own work with an agent or a tool: a log, a run, a mistake.

structure.name: Case
structure.purpose: Sentence 1: "My agent was supposed to X. Instead it did Y." with a number.

structure.name: Proof
structure.purpose: The log or the screen recording that shows it happened.

structure.name: Rule
structure.purpose: The one rule you use since then, as the punch line.

packaging_rules: Only real incidents from your own runs, with the log as proof.
title_formulas: My agent was supposed to X. It did Y
The one rule after my agent did X
formats.strong: Example format: documenting what already happened costs little, so the volume stays high.
